- **Purge stale run markers.** Delete any `{workflow.implementation_artifacts}/.escalation-*`, `{workflow.implementation_artifacts}/.on-escalation-fired-*`, `{workflow.implementation_artifacts}/.budget-*`, `{workflow.implementation_artifacts}/.heartbeat-*` and `{workflow.implementation_artifacts}/.stall-*` an earlier run left behind, before the hooks that write them are armed — a stale escalation marker makes this run look like it already escalated, a stale fired-marker silently swallows this run's first escalation ping, which is the one an absent operator is waiting on, and a stale turn counter is already at or past the ceiling, so the Stop hook escalates on this run's **first** Stop event before it has done a single turn of work — and a stale heartbeat's gap since the PRIOR run would fire this run's stall rule on its first resume about an idle nobody had. Those five dot-prefixed families only. **On a resume, purge nothing.** A resume re-asserts the environment rather than rebuilding it, and the turn counter is the one piece of that environment a resume must inherit: zeroing `.budget-*` on re-entry would hand an in-flight story a fresh ceiling every time it stopped, so a run could evade the budget indefinitely by resuming. A counter the operator has deliberately cleared is a different thing, and `/ucg-resolve` clears exactly that one when it closes a `budget-overrun` escalation. In particular do **not** delete `escalation-*.json`: the typed sidecar is an operator-facing artifact like `run-status.json` and `run-result.json`, neither of which is purged at arming either, and it is named per story rather than per run, so arming cannot tell a deliberately-pending sidecar from a stale one. A decision the operator chose to leave pending lives in exactly that file, and a prior run's unresolved escalation surfacing at `/ucg-resolve` is correct: it genuinely is still pending. Sidecar staleness is handled at read time instead, by the run-scoped marker scan in `references/execute.md`.
